Value-Added Analysis
http://projects.latimes.com/value-added/
A teacher’s value-added rating is based on his or her students’
progress on the California Standards Tests for English and
math. The difference between a student’s expected growth and
actual performance is the "value" a teacher added or subtracted
during the year. A school’s value-added rating is based on the
performance of all students tested there during that period.

Better phrased as the difference between a student’s
expected status and their actual status.
Whose “expectation”?

Contextual Value Added

Contextual Value Added (CVA) – Great Britain
CVA takes into account nine factors that are known to affect the perfor-
mance of children, but outside of the schools control. (From Wikipedia)
Gender
Special Educational Needs
Eligibility for free school meals.
First language
Whether pupils move between schools
Ethnicity
The age (i.e. the month they were born in) of different pupils within the
year group
Whether a pupil has been taken into care (e.g. Foster Care) at any
stage
The level of deprivation in the area the pupil lives (using the Income
Deprivation Affecting Children Index)
